guidance: Mix the weighting material through a hopper into the active system a little at a time and check the weight on a mud balance between additions, because a single pass rarely lands on the target and some barite always leaves with the cuttings at the shakers. Leave room in the pits for the volume the barite or the dilution fluid adds, and confirm the target weight against the drilling programme before mixing.
method: A mud weight change is a mass balance. One barrel holds 42 US gallons; fresh water weighs 8.33 lb/gal and drilling-grade barite is taken at 4.2 SG, or 35.0 lb/gal, so a barrel of solid barite weighs 1,470 lb and a 100 lb sack occupies 0.068 bbl. To raise the weight, pounds of barite = 1,470 x V x (W2 - W1) / (35 - W2) for a starting volume V in barrels, which is numerically the same as the count of 100 lb sacks per 100 bbl; the barite adds V x (W2 - W1) / (35 - W2) barrels, so the treated volume grows and the final weight is W2. To cut the weight, barrels of light fluid = V x (W1 - W2) / (W2 - Dw), where Dw is the dilution fluid density, 8.33 lb/gal for fresh water and the base-oil density for an oil-based mud, and the reported volume increase is that same quantity. Both branches are solved from the same balance, pounds in divided by gallons in, and the calculator reports the material, the final volume, the volume gain and the specific gravity (weight divided by 8.33). Inputs are limited to a current and target weight of 6 to 30 lb/gal, a volume of 0.1 to 100,000 bbl and a dilution fluid of 5 to 12 lb/gal; a target within 0.005 lb/gal of the current weight is reported as no change, and a dilution fluid at or above the target is refused because the balance has no solution. Warnings appear for a target above 20 lb/gal, a volume gain over 20 percent when weighting up, a dilution fluid within 0.5 lb/gal of the target, a dilution fluid below 8.0 lb/gal (a base oil rather than water) and dilution that adds more than 50 percent to the volume. The model assumes dry weighting material, no losses to the shakers or settling, one fully mixed volume measured at one temperature, and that the target weight is already permitted by the formation pressure, the equivalent circulating density and the mud programme; it does not model those limits or the effect on rheology and filtration, so the mixed weight still has to be verified on a mud balance.
